problem: CRIT-005's passThreshold requires: '...the record-earn/verify sub-path makes no LLM call (fail-closed if the config flips)'. run.sh:56-63 does have a fail-closed branch: 'if [ "${RECORD_EARN_USES_LLM:-1}" = "0" ]; then ... else echo ... refusing, fail-closed ... exit 1; fi'. But lib/config.sh:18 hard-assigns 'RECORD_EARN_USES_LLM=0' unconditionally on every source (not a conditional default like ': ${RECORD_EARN_USES_LLM:=0}'), and run.sh:28 unconditionally sources lib/config.sh at the very top BEFORE any test-mode branch runs. Consequently any RECORD_EARN_USES_LLM=1 an external caller or test tries to inject via the environment is immediately clobbered back to 0 by the source line -- the fail-closed branch at run.sh:61-62 is structurally unreachable through any normal invocation; it can only be exercised by editing the literal source text of lib/config.sh, which is not 'the config flipping' in any runtime sense. tests/test-prop9-model-policy.sh never attempts to set RECORD_EARN_USES_LLM=1 and observe the refusal (it only checks the config declares 0 and that a normal run emits the 'true' marker) -- so this untestable, dead branch is not caught by the test suite either. CRIT-005's own passThreshold ('fail-closed if the config flips') is therefore a claim that cannot be judged true or false against any artifact in this repo -- it fails this review's own dimension-1 binary-evaluability requirement.
fix: Either (a) change lib/config.sh:18 to a conditional default (': ${RECORD_EARN_USES_LLM:=0}') so an external override is actually observable, and add a test that sets RECORD_EARN_USES_LLM=1 in the environment before invoking run.sh in record_earn_only mode and asserts rc=1 + the refusal message, or (b) drop the 'fail-closed if the config flips' clause from CRIT-005's passThreshold since the current architecture makes it a config-file-editing scenario, not a runtime/env scenario, and is therefore not something Phase 3 can verify.
